transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... at the register at work, I keep getting stuck doing things that just don't fit the moment. Like, I'll be tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I just freeze with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting. 

Customers get so impatient now, you know? This one guy yesterday was buying six cans of creamed corn. Who eats that much creamed corn? My mother used to make it when I was a kid, but she'd put a little sugar in it. She lived in Ohio her whole life. The winters there get so cold, not like here, the snow would pile up past the porch steps. I haven't been back to Ohio since I finished my bachelor's degree... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right. The register. Yeah, because of the freezing and the tapping, last week it got me written up by my manager. So that's why I'm here.
When you get stuck tapping or freezing, does it feel like you have to do it to relieve a strong uncomfortable thought or feeling?

No, not really. I don't have an uncomfortable thought or anything I'm trying to get rid of. My hand just does it, or it just stops. 

My manager thinks I'm doing it on purpose, though. He wears these awful ties, like bright yellow with little golf clubs all over them. I don't even know why people play golf, to be honest. You just hit a little white ball around a giant lawn. My neighbor has a lawn that he mows twice a week, every Tuesday and Saturday, right at 7 AM. The mower is so loud, it wakes up all the stray cats on our street. There's this one orange tabby that always sleeps right under my car tire, so I have to check before I leave for work... wait, did you ask me about the register again?
Before your hand taps or freezes, do you feel a brief urge or pressure that builds up and is relieved when it happens?

No, it's not like an urge or a pressure building up. It just... happens. But speaking of pressure, the water pressure in my apartment has been absolutely terrible lately. I keep trying to get my landlord to fix it, but he's always busy tinkering with his antique cars in the garage. He has this old Ford, I think it's from the 1950s, painted cherry red. My uncle had a red truck when I was growing up. We used to ride in the back of it during the summer, eating watermelon and spitting the seeds over the side. You can't even buy good watermelon anymore, you know? It's all seedless now and it just tastes like water. I bought one at the grocery store where I work last week, and it was completely mushy inside. The produce section there is always freezing cold, though. They keep the air conditioning cranked so high the lettuce practically frosts over... wait, what did you ask me? Something about pressure?
Since childhood, have conversations often gone off track like this for you?

No, I don't really think it's been like this since I was a kid. I was actually pretty focused back then. I liked school a lot, especially geography. We had this big globe in the back of the classroom, and I'd just spin it and put my finger down to see where I landed. One time I landed on Madagascar. They have those lemurs there, you know, the ones with the black and white striped tails. 

I saw them at the zoo once with my niece. She dropped her cotton candy right in the dirt that day, and she cried for like twenty minutes straight. Cotton candy is just spun sugar anyway, it's terrible for your teeth. My dentist is always telling me I need to floss more, but the floss always shreds between my back molars. I think I need to buy that flat tape kind instead of the regular string. They sell it at the pharmacy next to the grocery store where I work, but the line there is always so long because they only ever have one person working the register... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Something about when I was a kid?
Have you been feeling unusually energized or high lately?

No, not really. I don't feel energized or high or anything like that. Just regular, I guess. I do drink a fair amount of coffee, though, just to get through my shifts at the register. I buy this dark roast from a little cafe down the street from my place. The barista there always spells my name wrong on the cup. It's not even a hard name, but she adds all these extra letters. 

People just don't pay attention to spelling anymore. When I got my bachelor's degree, they actually spelled my middle name wrong on the diploma itself. It took the university six months to mail me a replacement, and by then I had already moved out of my old apartment. Moving is such a nightmare, packing all those cardboard boxes. I always run out of packing tape right when I'm in the middle of the kitchen. And the clear tape is the absolute worst because you can never find the edge when it sticks back to the roll. You just sit there picking at it with your fingernail for ten minutes, and when you finally get a piece, it tears diagonally... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my coffee?
Do you hear voices when no one else is there?

Yeah, actually, most days I do. I hear what sounds like a couple of people talking just off to the side of me. Sometimes they're calling my name from the stockroom, or they'll say I rang something up wrong, but when I turn around there’s nobody there and no one else heard it. 

Speaking of ringing things up, the registers at my store are so ancient. The buttons stick all the time, especially the double-zero key. You have to press it exactly in the middle or it doesn't work. We had a repair guy come in last month, but he just sprayed some compressed air in it and left. Compressed air is getting so expensive, though. I used to buy it all the time to clean my computer keyboard back when I had this massive desktop PC. It took up half my desk. Desks are so heavy to move, especially the solid wood ones. I helped my buddy move an oak desk down three flights of stairs once, and my back hasn't been the same since. You really have to lift with your knees, but it's hard on a narrow staircase. The handrails in his building were completely loose, just wobbling everywhere... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Something about the stockroom?
